about.title: Personal Injury Help in Lafayette, California
about.longDescription: Lafayette sits along the SR-24 corridor, a stretch that carries heavy commuter traffic between the Caldecott Tunnel and points east — and that traffic shows up in the numbers. In the most recent full year on record, Lafayette saw 106 injury collisions and 142 people hurt, with one traffic death. Crashes here tend to cluster on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m., a pattern that lines up with SR-24, SR-24 Eastbound, and SR-24 Westbound as the corridors with the highest recorded collision counts. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, or in any other kind of accident around town, you're likely dealing with medical bills, missed work, and a lot of uncertainty about what comes next. We handle personal injury cases for residents in Lafayette and throughout Contra Costa County. Our team can review what happened and explain your options — at no cost to you. We only get paid if you recover compensation. You don't have to figure this out on your own.

items.title: You Have Two Years — But Don't Wait
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim, though claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Getting started early helps preserve evidence while it's still fresh.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Shut the Door
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still pursue compensation even if you were partly responsible for the accident. Any recovery is simply adjusted to reflect your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain-and-Suffering Damages
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no limit on non-economic damages like pain and suffering. That means your claim can reflect the full extent of what you've been through, not an arbitrary ceiling.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to have your case reviewed. You only pay a fee if we recover compensation on your behalf.

items.question: How much does it cost to get a case review?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer free case reviews, and there's no obligation. If you hire us, we work on contingency, meaning you pay no fee unless we recover compensation for you.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an accident in Lafayette?
items.answer: In most personal injury cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the accident to file a claim. If a government entity is involved, such as a city vehicle or a defect on public property, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so it's wise to look into your options sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if the accident was partly my fault?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame for the accident. Your total recovery would just be reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated entirely.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Lafayette?
items.answer: Public collision records show that reported injury crashes in Lafayette are most frequently associated with the SR-24 corridor, including its eastbound and westbound segments. Crash reports also tend to peak on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m., which lines up with heavier commute traffic — this is simply a pattern in the public record, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Is there a limit on how much I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: No. California does not cap non-economic damages, such as pain and suffering, in typical personal injury cases. This differs from some other types of claims, like certain medical malpractice cases, where different rules may apply.
